mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in each of the last four weeks (-13.6 to -20.0). This autocorrelated momentum reflects persistent behavioral caution or habit formation that will continue to suppress retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks without any new intervening shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days despite the four-week declining streak, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved sharply from -9.9 to -4.4 over four weeks. Once WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -5.0, the restored commuting pattern generates incidental lunchtime and after-work retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -5.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -9.9 at t-3w to -4.4 at t-0w, crossing -5.0 in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues declining for two weeks after WORKPLACES crosses above -5.0, the threshold trigger is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in TRANSIT (flat-to-rising, 2.7 to 2.6 with intra-period peak at 3.1) and WORKPLACES (-9.9 to -4.4) together signal a compounding return-to-commute ecosystem: more people using transit to reach workplaces increases en-route exposure to retail corridors, raising RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show net improvement over the four-week window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both continue to improve jointly, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined from -11.9 to -17.9 over four weeks, consistent with rising pre-summer heat in Delhi in March reducing outdoor park visits. As park usage drops, displaced leisure demand shifts to air-conditioned retail and recreation venues, producing a short-term rise in RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 5 points below its t-3w level
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined by 6.0 points from t-3w (-11.9) to t-0w (-17.9)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline alongside falling PARKS mobility rather than rising, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has steadily declined from 17.6 to 10.7, indicating that pandemic-driven essential-goods stockpiling behavior induced by earlier restrictions is normalizing as policy restrictions ease. This normalization frees household mobility budgets for discretionary retail and recreation trips over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 17.6 at t-3w to 10.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues falling despite the continued decline in GROCERY_PHARM excess mobility, the normalization-substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen from 4.1 to 5.1 over four weeks. If this upward trend in time-at-home persists for two consecutive weeks above 5.0, it signals a behavioral shift toward home-centric routines that will suppress RETAIL_REC over the following week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 5.0 for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 5.6 at t-2w and remained elevated at 5.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week following two consecutive weeks of RESIDENTIAL above 5.0, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility is recovering strongly (-9.9 to -4.4) while TRANSIT mobility remains nearly flat (2.7 to 2.6), suggesting transit capacity or policy restrictions are not scaling with workplace reopening. This mismatch creates commuting friction (crowding, limited transit options) that discourages ancillary retail trips, dragging RETAIL_REC down over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 5.5 points while TRANSIT rose only 0.1 point over the same four-week window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks despite the persistent gap between WORKPLACES recovery and flat TRANSIT, the friction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in PARKS mobility through mid-March in Delhi reflects the seasonal transition toward hotter daytime temperatures that historically reduce outdoor activity citywide, including retail footfall tied to outdoor markets and open-air shopping areas, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined every week from -11.9 to -17.9 over the snapshot period
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while PARKS continues to decline due to seasonal heat, the seasonal suppression hypothesis is rejected.
